timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This is Day 3 of our Labs of Democracy 2022 and we are in the beautiful state of New Jersey.
On this side, we are seeing the beautiful skyline of New York.
We have been in Princeton. We have seen many things and you have had some very intense discussions
with other state legislators on climate and energy policies. What do you take away so far?
I think if we want to fight climate change, we have to find a global approach.
So it's very important to talk to just both sides of the Atlantic and just to exchange ideas and thoughts
and different issues we have in different states and so on.
So that's very important. That's what I am taking from here to back home.
That it's not that easy but I think we can manage it.
Climate and energy plays an important role also in your legislative agenda.
Tell us a little bit about the state you come from and why you believe climate and energy policy is so important right now.
Baden Rutenberg is a very industrial state so we have to find a way to bring our whole energy supply to renewable bases.
And that's quite tough because even right now we don't have enough sources for our own powers.
We have to import all the electricity and now we want to build up even more renewable power plants and that's quite difficult task.
And we have to find a way to bring all the industries to a more climate neutral, carbon neutral way of production otherwise.
All the workforce will just be deployed.
You had the opportunity to talk to state legislators from all parties also Republicans and Democrats.
The social Democrats at home, the FDT, the Greens, the CDU. Is that common ground?
I think there is common ground on the goal like reaching the goals from the Paris Agreement.
But we are heavily discussing about the way how to get there.
But it's quite fun and it's helping to have this exchange because it's kind of off the normal party politics right here.
So we can just exchange our ideas on a less political way just more based on the facts.
And why in a transatlantic way?
Well I think the US is a very important partner in the Western world.
And so I think if the US and the states in the US are going on the way to more climate neutral or carbon neutral way of life,
then it can be kind of an example for others to follow.
And that's why it's so important to have this transatlantic exchange.
Thank you so much.
Thank you.

youtube_description:
As part of Aspen Germany's Laboratories of Democracy Initiative, the 2022 cohort met in New Jersey from September 13 to September 17, 2022. Each year, the project brings together a group of German and U.S. state legislators for two study tours – one to Germany and one to the United States – and virtual meetings. The goal of the project is to promote values-based dialogue and exchange of ideas on common policy challenges at the subnational level. Climate and energy were at the forefront of the 2022 round of exchanges.

We used the opportunity to interview the participating state legislators from the United States and Germany 🇺🇸🇩🇪. Why are they involved in transatlantic relations? Why are they participating in this Aspen program? Why is the topic of climate and energy important to them and their work? What have they learned from this exchange and their visit to New Jersey?

🗣️ Watch to the conversation between Daniel Karrais MdL (FDP), Member of the State Parliament of Baden-Württemberg, and our Executive Director Dr. Stormy-Annika Mildner.

To learn more about the program, visit our website: https://www.aspeninstitute.de/events/laboratories-of-democracy-initiative-meeting-of-2022-cohort-in-new-jersey/.

The project is supported by the Transatlantic Program of the Federal Republic of Germany with funds from the European Recovery Program (ERP) of the Federal Ministry of Economics and Climate Protection (BMWK).
